Thousands of devotees gathered for the event, which began with a procession.  Special masses and a holy car procession are scheduled during the eleven-day celebration.  Over a million devotees are expected to visit the shrine during this period.

title: Nepal flash floods: How a tea break saved lives of 5 Chhattisgarh friends
description: Five friends from Raipur found themselves in a life-threatening situation in Nepal when they narrowly escaped flash floods. A timely tea break allowed them to stay clear of the destruction caused by the surging Trishuli river, which swept away vehicles and debris. Huddled in safety for two anxious days, they eventually returned home without harm, relieved and thankful.

title: ‘I urge others to speak up’: Ex-Pak cricketer's emotional appeal for Imran Khan

International captains have also called for adequate healthcare and constitutional safeguards. Greg Chappell described Imran Khan's condition as worrying and difficult to ascertain. The Pakistan Cricket Board lodged a complaint after an interview with Imran Khan's sons aired.

title: Flood fears in Bihar as several rivers cross danger marks amid Nepal rains
description: Bihar faces intensified flood fears as river water levels rise significantly. Persistent rains in Nepal and the state have caused rivers to exceed danger marks. The Gandak river has breached its danger level, releasing substantial water downstream. Authorities have moved residents from low-lying areas and placed departments on alert. District magistrates are personally monitoring the escalating flood situation across vulnerable regions.

title: John Cena reveals he and The Rock ‘hated each other’ before WrestleMania showdown
description: John Cena openly acknowledged the animosity that brewed before his WrestleMania 28 clash with The Rock. Their competitive rivalry escalated beyond the ring, leading to personal jabs and near confrontations backstage during heated promo exchanges. Although Cena publicly insisted he would prevail, he privately recognized The Rock's impending victory. After the match, heartfelt apologies paved the way for a newfound respect between the two icons.

title: ‘A little jealous’: Sunil Chhetri on India’s chance to play Brazil, Uruguay
description: Sunil Chhetri, the revered former captain, expresses a nuanced envy as he observes the current Indian football team gearing up for matches against legendary opponents like Brazil and Uruguay. He emphasises the importance of these unique encounters and encourages young players to make the most of this chance. Chhetri has confidence in the coach's choices and urges a united front for a brighter future in Indian football.

title: Trump vs Carney: Cars, homes, booze and more caught in US-Canada tariff war
description: The recent imposition of new tariffs on vehicles and construction materials has intensified the trade conflict between the US and Canada. This has also led to surging import taxes on other household products and alcoholic beverages. Both businesses and consumers are likely to feel the pinch with escalating costs, potentially affecting employment rates. Moreover, these disputes cast a shadow of uncertainty over the USMCA trade agreement.

title: BFSI firms drive India’s GCC office leasing as demand shifts beyond tech
description: In a notable development, foreign BFSI companies ramped up their leasing activities for global centers in India, resulting in a remarkable seventy percent year-on-year rise. Conversely, foreign IT-ITeS firms have cut back on office space absorption. The commercial real estate market in India reflects changing dynamics, with other service and manufacturing sectors displaying distinct trends in their leasing decisions.

title: Karnataka HC slams cops over activist’s ‘illegal arrest’ in Kunal Kamra show cancellation
description: The Karnataka High Court has raised serious concerns over the alleged unlawful detention of an activist by the Whitefield Police. Noting a pattern of procedural violations at the station, the court highlighted that the activist was apprehended following a Facebook post celebrating a canceled show. The police initiated action under a suo motu case, lacking a formal complaint, prompting authorities to demand clarifications on these irregularities.

title: ‘He could be in the realms of Lara and Tendulkar’: Boycott’s big Brook warning
description: Sir Geoffrey Boycott has high praise for Harry Brook's exceptional batting skills but expresses concern that Brook isn't fully harnessing his potential in Test cricket. He believes Brook's style is too reminiscent of white-ball play, suggesting it could hinder his development. Boycott sees similarities between Brook and legendary players like Lara and Tendulkar but laments that his advice went unheeded.

title: After Bombay HC rap, FDA withdraws orders against Cipla, MCA eateries
description: The Bombay High Court took a firm stance against the Maharashtra FDA, rebuking its treatment of Cipla and five eateries. The court underscored that the FDA's decisions compromised natural justice and displayed an inflexible approach. With the court's direction, the FDA rescinded its suspension of the Mumbai Cricket Association restaurants and reinstated Cipla's drug sale licence. The court called on the FDA to practice due diligence in its enforcement strategies.

title: What does Tom Brady keep from every Super Bowl win? The answer is on his phone
description: Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, but one of his most personal collections lives on his phone. The former NFL quarterback revealed that he created separate folders for his championship victories and saved congratulatory messages sent after each one. The habit has preserved a private record of a career that included 10 Super Bowl appearances and five Super Bowl MVP awards.

title: The deadly forces behind Nepal’s Himalayan disasters
description: In Langtang National Park, a large ice and rock collapse triggered a severe flooding incident, revealing Nepal's ongoing struggle with natural disasters intensified by climate change. Rapid urban growth and human activities exacerbate exposure to these perilous weather events. Although the government has taken steps to bolster disaster management, glaring weaknesses in early warning systems persist. To better manage risks, the country must focus on improved monitoring and stronger infrastructure.

title: Haiti gang frees 13 women and children days after raid that killed at least 47 people
description: A gang in Haiti has freed thirteen hostages, including women and children, following a brutal assault. UNICEF played a crucial role in securing their release from a farming community. This incident in Kenscoff underscores the rampant violence impacting children across Haiti. The region has faced numerous fatalities and displacement due to gang activities, although mass abductions are less frequent and often yield unpredictable results for those abducted.

Police arrived and attempted to persuade her to step away from the railing. A passerby intervened and successfully pulled her away from the edge. The incident, stemming from a family dispute, was resolved safely.

title: From 5 days to just 2: Ex-England captain explains why Tests are getting shorter
description: Test matches are wrapping up more swiftly than they did in earlier years. The rise of aggressive T20-style batting and enhanced performances from fast bowlers are driving this trend. Additionally, the preparation of bowler-friendly pitches for the World Test Championship and the impact of DRS technology on umpiring decisions, particularly LBWs, are significant factors. Statistics reveal a noticeable increase in matches concluding within a three-day timeframe.

As a result, they are required to provide corrective action plans to address these violations and ensure compliance with food safety regulations.

This unexpected decision follows claims of contract infractions associated with Musk's enterprises, notably Twitter and xAI. OpenAI has expressed concerns about SpaceX's adherence to its service terms, resulting in Cursor losing model access by November 2026. Meanwhile, discussions are underway between SpaceX and OpenAI to find a resolution to the ongoing conflict.

title: 22 girls accuse school helper of molestation at Thane tribal school, arrested
description: A school helper faces new molestation allegations from twenty-two minor girls. He was previously jailed for a similar offense and released on bail. Police are investigating how he secured employment after his earlier arrest. The accused allegedly took advantage of girls' movements within the school. Authorities have registered a case and arrested the suspect.

title: Fuel paradox: Russia has oil, so why is it importing petrol from India?
description: Russian petrol stations are rationing fuel due to Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries.  These strikes have disrupted domestic fuel supplies, causing shortages across the nation.  Russia is now importing finished petrol from countries like India to meet demand.  This unusual trade flow highlights the difference between crude production and refining capacity.  The ongoing refinery damage strains Russia's energy system supporting its economy.

title: H-1B workers' 60-day grace period may end: What happens next
description: The US Department of Homeland Security is considering a proposal that may eliminate the 60-day grace period for foreign workers, particularly affecting H-1B visa holders and countless Indian professionals. This grace period currently allows individuals to seek new jobs or modify their status before needing to leave the US. Without it in place, workers may face immediate departure following job loss, with final details pending further evaluation.

title: Jamie Dimon says it is ‘frustrating’ to hear America is behind in defence tech
description: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon voiced frustration regarding US defense technology perceptions.  The bank launched a $1.5 trillion Security and Resiliency Initiative for national security industries.  This program now includes Canada, Europe, and the United Kingdom.  The initiative supports aerospace, defense, manufacturing, energy, and health tech sectors.  The bank is investing significant capital and personnel into this critical effort.

title: Rebuilding after devastating floods may cost Nepal nearly 10% of its economy
description: Nepal's finance minister estimates flood reconstruction costs between four and five billion dollars.  This devastating flood killed over 600 people and left thousands missing.  The disaster destroyed towns, bridges, roads, and damaged hydropower stations significantly.  Search and rescue operations continue despite disruptions from bad weather conditions.  India has provided substantial relief materials to the affected regions.

title: 'Grateful for special gesture': PM Modi thanks Uzbek prez for warm welcome
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi began a four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. He will hold bilateral talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent. Modi will then attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. This visit aims to strengthen India's strategic partnerships in Central Asia. The summit will bring together leaders from ten member nations.
